recommendations: Do not swap pycolmap out yet: none of the direct-equirect papers use COLMAP for pose recovery (it has no spherical/equirectangular camera model) — they use OpenMVG (OmniGS, ODGS) or OpenSfM (the hobby recipe below). Adopting direct-equirect training means also replacing the SfM stage, which is a bigger, riskier pipeline change than it first appears for only 20 outdoor stills.

If you want to prototype direct-from-equirect training, start from esw0116/ODGS (MIT, NeurIPS 2024) rather than OmniGS (GPL-3.0, heavier CUDA/LibTorch/OpenCV-CUDA native build) — ODGS is Python/PyTorch-ish, permissively licensed, and closer to your existing gsplat/Brush stack, but expect a stale repo (no commits since Dec 2024) and the need to wire in OpenMVG for poses yourself.

Treat SC-OmniGS, Spherical-GOF, ErpGS, and TPGS as watch-only for now: each claims strong outdoor or pose-free results but has no runnable public training code as of July 2026 (SC-OmniGS repo is a project webpage only; Spherical-GOF repo has just README+LICENSE with code 'will be released'; ErpGS project page literally says 'Code (Coming Soon)'; TPGS repo has 17 commits but an incomplete README with no working setup instructions).

Skip the feed-forward pair methods (PanSplat, Splatter-360, OmniSplat) for this goal — they solve 2-view interpolation/generalization, not fusing ~20 wide-baseline stills into one consistent walkable scene, and are validated mainly on indoor synthetic benchmarks (Matterport3D, HM3D, Replica). PanSplat's Insta360-video fine-tune is the most real-world-relevant checkpoint of the three but is still pairwise, not a full-scene reconstruction from N stills.

Best low-risk experiment: keep your current pycolmap perspective-crop SfM exactly as-is (it is proven on outdoor unbounded scenes), but aggregate the recovered per-crop poses back into one pose per source equirect frame and feed that into an ODGS/OmniGS-style equirect rasterizer for the final gsplat training pass instead of the resampled perspective crops. This captures the no-crop-seam benefit of direct-equirect training without abandoning the SfM stage that already works for you.

Warn the user up front that 20 stills is sparse for a large outdoor scene (a bridge plus surrounding roadways): every panorama-GS paper surveyed here demonstrates on dozens-to-hundreds of frames or continuous video, not ~20 discrete stills. Recommend either capturing more panoramas spaced along the roadway/under the deck, or leaning on a monocular-depth prior (as LighthouseGS, ErpGS, and the hobbyist SPAG4d tool do) to regularize the sparse regions, regardless of which splat variant is ultimately used.

For a quick practical spike (not a citation-grade research contribution), inuex35/360-gaussian-splatting is the closest existing recipe to 'N equirect stills -> OpenSfM spherical poses -> panorama-aware 3DGS training' end to end, and worth cloning to see how far it gets on a bridge dataset before investing in any of the CVPR/ICLR papers above — but it is an unpublished hobby repo with unverified maintenance state, so budget time for debugging.
slice: Papers/code that train 3D Gaussian Splatting directly from equirectangular/360 panoramas (no perspective-crop preprocessing) — OmniGS, 360-GS, ODGS, Splatter-360, PanSplat, OmniSplat, ErpGS, PanoGS, TPGS, and newer 2026 work
summary: Direct-from-equirect 3DGS is an active but still academic-maturity field as of July 2026. Real, runnable, per-scene optimization code exists for OmniGS (WACV 2025, GPL-3.0, C++/CUDA equirect rasterizer) and ODGS (NeurIPS 2024, MIT, PyTorch) — both require poses from OpenMVG, not COLMAP, since COLMAP has no spherical camera model. 360-GS (Feb 2024) also has public code (LeoDarcy/360GS) using tangent-plane projection with a custom panorama rasterizer, indoor-focused. The self-calibrating/pose-free option that would most help a sparse-still capture, SC-OmniGS (ICLR 2025), has only a project webpage on GitHub, not training code. Newer 2026 work (Spherical-GOF, CylinderSplat, UniTriSplat, PFGS360, ODGS-SLAM) pushes geometry quality and pose-freeness further but is either code-not-yet-released, video-sequence-oriented (not discrete stills), or unverified in this research pass. ErpGS and TPGS address outdoor 360-rig distortion and single-panorama reconstruction respectively, but ErpGS's code is "coming soon" and TPGS's repo is incomplete/undocumented. Feed-forward generalizable methods (Splatter-360, PanSplat, OmniSplat) are the most code-complete and well-maintained (pretrained checkpoints, active repos), but solve 2-view interpolation for indoor synthetic benchmarks, not many-view outdoor scene fusion. SPaGS (EGSR/CGF 2025) is notable for an explicit outdoor drone-panorama dataset but ships as a plugin to a heavyweight research framework. Bottom line: perspective-split remains the practical route for Orbit Studio today, primarily because it lets you keep COLMAP for pose recovery; direct-equirect training is promising but not a drop-in replacement.

sources.title: GitHub - liquorleaf/OmniGS: [WACV 2025] OmniGS: Fast Radiance Field Reconstruction using Omnidirectional Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: GPU-accelerated omnidirectional rasterizer splats 3D Gaussians directly onto equirectangular screen space, no cubemap/tangent-plane approximation needed
License is GPL-3.0
Requires known camera poses (longitude-latitude format), demonstrated on 360Roam and EgoNeRF datasets via openMVG-style formatting
79 stars, 10 forks, 5 open issues, 17 commits, no formal releases as of research date
Build requires CUDA 11.8, cuDNN 8.9.3, OpenCV 4.7.0 (CUDA-built), LibTorch 2.0.1 — native C++ build, not a simple pip install
quotes: there exists some unknown bug for this function

sources.title: GitHub - esw0116/ODGS: [NeurIPS 2024] ODGS: 3D Scene Reconstruction from Omnidirectional Images with 3D Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: MIT licensed
Poses obtained via OpenMVG Structure-from-Motion, not COLMAP, for all 6 evaluated datasets
Evaluated on OmniBlender, Ricoh360, OmniPhotos, 360Roam, OmniScenes, and 360VO datasets (mix of indoor and driving-style capture)
Claims 100x faster optimization/rendering than NeRF-based omnidirectional baselines
Last commit December 26, 2024 — no activity in the ~19 months since

sources.title: GitHub - chenyingshu/sc-omnigs: [ICLR 2025] SC-OmniGS: Self-Calibrating Omnidirectional Gaussian Splatting - Web Page
key_claims: Jointly optimizes 3D Gaussians, omnidirectional camera poses, and camera model without requiring precomputed poses — treats 360 images as a full sphere rather than converting to cube maps
The GitHub repo is a project webpage only (58.8% CSS, 22.6% JS, 18.6% HTML) — no training code is present, only a link out to a separate project site
10 commits total, all webpage-related; no license file found in the repo

sources.title: GitHub - thucz/splatter360: [CVPR 2025] Splatter-360: Generalizable 360 Gaussian Splatting for Wide-baseline Panoramic Images
key_claims: Feed-forward generalizable method: builds a spherical cost volume via spherical sweep, demonstrated to transfer zero-shot from HM3D-trained weights to Replica dataset scenes without per-scene optimization
Pretrained checkpoints released via Google Drive, plus training/eval/preprocessing scripts
26 commits, 7 open issues; license file could not be located (404 on direct LICENSE fetch)
Trained and evaluated on synthetic indoor datasets HM3D and Replica, not outdoor scenes

sources.title: GitHub - chengzhag/PanSplat: [CVPR'25] PanSplat: 4K Panorama Synthesis with Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: MIT licensed, most actively maintained repo of the feed-forward panorama methods surveyed (last commit March 25, 2025, bug fix to WS-PSNR eval)
Core method takes two wide-baseline 360 panoramas as input; uses a spherical 3D Gaussian pyramid with Fibonacci lattice arrangement
Pretrained checkpoints released at 512x1024 (Matterport3D, indoor synthetic) and 2048x4096 (4K, needs 24GB+ VRAM), plus fine-tunes on real-world 360Loc and custom Insta360 video footage
Two-step deferred backpropagation reduces memory footprint enough to train at 4K on a single A100

sources.title: GitHub - esw0116/OmniSplat: [CVPR 2025] OmniSplat: Taming Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Omnidirectional Images with Editable Capabilities
key_claims: MIT licensed; feed-forward, built on top of MVSplat using its pretrained re10k.ckpt without fine-tuning
Decomposes omnidirectional images into a Yin-Yang grid for stable cross-view attention, and separates scene elements into editable components
First code upload was June 6, 2025, so the codebase is only about a year old and self-described as early-stage
Authors acknowledge a known pixel-misalignment bug during omnidirectional image warping requiring a manual patch to an external library
quotes: There will be a pixel misalignment during the omnidirectional image warping

sources.title: GitHub - zhijieshen-bjtu/TPGS (You Need a Transition Plane: Bridging Continuous Panoramic 3D Reconstruction with Perspective Gaussian Splatting)
key_claims: Reconstructs 3D from a single equirectangular panorama via cubemap decomposition, adding a 'transition plane' between adjacent cube faces to remove stitching seams
MIT licensed, 17 commits, 2 open issues, no releases published
README is incomplete: dependency list, setup instructions, and dataset-prep steps are missing or reference external docs only, despite the paper claiming code and models are available

sources.title: ErpGS: Equirectangular Image Rendering enhanced with 3D Gaussian Regularization (project page)
key_claims: Targets distortion and rig-obstacle artifacts specific to equirectangular multi-view capture via geometric regularization, scale regularization, and distortion-aware masking
As of the research date, code is explicitly not yet released
Qualitative results shown on the project page and OmniBlender ablation dataset appear to be indoor scenes only; no outdoor examples were found

sources.title: GitHub - 1170632760/Spherical-GOF (Spherical-GOF: Geometry-Aware Panoramic Gaussian Opacity Fields for 3D Scene Reconstruction)
key_claims: Performs Gaussian Opacity Field ray sampling directly on the unit sphere rather than via projection-based rasterization, claiming 57% depth-reprojection-error reduction and 21% cycle-inlier-ratio improvement over the strongest baseline
MIT licensed, but the repo currently contains only .gitignore, LICENSE, README, and an assets folder — 2 commits total, no source implementation files
References a forthcoming 'OmniRob' dataset that is also not yet released

sources.title: GitHub - nerficg-project/SPaGS (SPaGS: Fast and Accurate 3D Gaussian Splatting for Spherical Panoramas, Computer Graphics Forum 2025)
key_claims: MIT licensed; ships as a plugin/module for the separate 'NeRFICG' research framework (installed via ./scripts/install.py -m SPaGS), not a standalone repo
Introduces exact axis-aligned bounding box calculation for spherical images to speed up omnidirectional ray casting of 3D Gaussians

Ships a new 'RaR' (Roaming and Rounding) dataset with real outdoor drone-captured scenes (named O_car, O_lion, O_statuary, O_stone, O_windmill) that pair panoramic and simultaneous perspective captures
Only 1 commit recorded in the SPaGS-specific repo, reflecting its dependency on the larger parent framework

sources.title: CylinderSplat: 3D Gaussian Splatting with Cylindrical Triplanes for Panoramic Novel View Synthesis (arXiv / ICLR 2026)
key_claims: Introduces a cylindrical Triplane representation aligned to panoramic/Manhattan-world geometry, with a dual-branch pixel + volume architecture to handle occlusions in sparse-view panoramic capture
Explicitly designed to flexibly handle a variable number of input views, from a single panorama up to multiple panoramas, which is closer to Orbit Studio's ~20-still use case than pairwise methods
Paper references code at github.com/wangqww/CylinderSplat, but actual repo contents/completeness were not independently verified in this research pass
Accepted as an ICLR 2026 conference paper

sources.title: GitHub - inuex35/360-gaussian-splatting
key_claims: Hobbyist end-to-end recipe: runs OpenSfM (bin/opensfm_run_all) with a spherical camera model on a folder of 360 photos to produce a reconstruction.json, then trains a modified 3DGS with a --panorama training flag
Explicitly chosen because COLMAP does not support the spherical/equirectangular camera model needed for direct pose recovery from 360 stills
Vendors diff-gaussian-rasterization and simple-knn submodules and offers multiple render modes including an OmniGS-style omnidirectional renderer
README recommends a smaller densify_grad_threshold (0.00002) specifically for equirectangular projections due to increased memory demands
